question: Why does this composition of meaning not serve a merely personal purpose despite arising from the seed of the Veda and its lord?
premises: The composition does not go for its own purpose.
It is a composition of meaning.
It is linked to the seed of the Veda and so forth of the lord.
inference: The speech's meaning-structure is not self-serving but rooted in a transcendent scriptural source.
uncertainties: The exact relation between īśituḥ and bīja is compactly expressed.
plain_english: Whose composition of meaning does not go for its own sake, being of the lord who is the seed of the Veda and so forth.
